notes: EBIT is modeled as 'Income from operations' from the consolidated statements (GAAP operating income), which includes items affecting comparability (including impairments) as presented in the filings.

D&A is computed as depreciation expense + amortization of intangibles + other amortization expense (all from FY2025 10-K cash flow / supplemental line items). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001418135/000141813526000016/kdp-20251231.htm))

Capex is modeled as 'Purchases of property, plant, and equipment' from the cash flow statement (absolute dollars, not in millions). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001418135/000141813526000016/kdp-20251231.htm))

NWC definition for this package: (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents − restricted cash and restricted cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − short-term borrowings and current portion of long-term obligations). Structured payables are treated as operating current liabilities (not interest-bearing debt) and remain inside current liabilities.

2026 revenue forecast is acquisition-sensitive and uses the midpoint of KDP’s stated 2026 net sales guidance ($25.9B-$26.4B) from the FY2025 release; FY2027-FY2030 fade assumptions are not explicitly guided in the release and are modeled to be directionally conservative. ([news.keurigdrpepper.com](https://news.keurigdrpepper.com/2026-02-24-Keurig-Dr-Pepper-Reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-Results-and-Provides-2026-Outlook))
WACC is a modeling assumption for the DCF package (not disclosed as a single value in the cited sections) and is set to 0.079 as a baseline sensitivity anchor.

Terminal exit EBITDA multiple (11.5) and NTM comp multiples were not fully sourced from primary databases during this run; terminal values are therefore assumption-driven and should be sensitivity-tested.

Preferred equity and minority interest are set to null because the FY2025 balance sheet presented in the 10-K shows no non-controlling interest balance and preferred equity issuance timing appears tied to subsequent transaction events; verify post-balance-sheet capitalization if modeling the post-separation structure.
NOL utilization percent is set to null because the 10-K provides tax-effected NOL carryforwards amounts but does not provide a direct utilization rate assumption suitable for DCF cash tax modeling.

catalysts: Timing and integration of the JDE Peet's transaction contribution in 2026 and execution of the planned separation into two public companies.
Credit/debt management around the transaction (refinancing, leverage trajectory) and related impacts on equity risk premium/WACC perception.
Operational levers (net price realization, productivity savings, and volume/mix management) that could move EBIT margins toward/away from base case.
company_overview: Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) is a coffee and beverage company in North America that manufactures, markets, distributes, and sells hot and cold beverages and single-serve brewing systems.
KDP reports consolidated results driven by net sales and operating income, with meaningful D&A and ongoing capital investment to support manufacturing and distribution capabilities.

The company carries equity method investments (e.g., operating partnerships/joint investments) and has sizeable interest-bearing obligations, resulting in structurally lower net working capital typical for packaged beverages.
current_context: In the FY2025 results release (Feb 24, 2026), KDP guided 2026 net sales of $25.9B-$26.4B and described low-double-digit constant-currency adjusted diluted EPS growth, including incremental contribution from the anticipated JDE Peet's transaction.

KDP also reported FY2025 GAAP operating income of $962M and FY2025 adjusted operating income totaling 30.9% of net sales (as described in the release), while discussing inflationary and volume/mix headwinds in the year-over-year comparisons.
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is anchored to the 2026 net sales guidance range midpoint, then fades into a more moderate growth profile over FY2027-FY2030 to reflect normalization after the near-term transaction impact.

Base-case EBIT margin assumptions reflect a path from FY2025 operating profitability toward a steady-state margin level, consistent with the company’s historical ability to manage productivity and cost efficiency amid inflationary pressure.
D&A and capex are modeled using historical ratios (from FY2023-FY2025) to keep reinvestment intensity economically consistent with the asset base and maintenance/capacity capex needs.
Working capital is modeled as persistently negative (payables-funded), with gradual improvement toward a more stable negative level, reflecting the packaged-beverage business cash conversion cycle.
key_risks: Execution risk around acquisition integration and subsequent separation, including cost overruns, timing slippage, and potential margin volatility.
Macro risks (inflation and foreign exchange) that may pressure volume/mix and net price realization, impacting operating margins.
Working-capital variability (including structured payables and supplier/receivable terms) could materially deviate from assumed negative NWC levels.

valuation_summary: The DCF build uses explicit revenue, margin, and cash investment drivers with terminal economics set via an exit multiple method (exit EBITDA multiple) and a conservative terminal growth rate.
The base-case chain is QA-friendly: forecast revenue each year is directly derived from the provided growth series starting with FY2025 net sales.
Scenario overrides are intentionally modest (growth/margin and WACC/terminal assumptions), suitable for sensitivity analysis rather than promotional forecasting.
